subject: physics
question_text: A man walks on a straight road from his home to a market 2.5 km away with a speed of 5 km/h. Finding the market closed, he instantly turns and walks back home with a speed of 7.5 km/h. What is (a) the magnitude of the average velocity and (b) the average speed of the man over the interval 0 to 50 min?

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), VERY SHORT ANSWER 9 of Unit 4. The mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for Unit 4, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Average velocity
lines: 2.5/7.5 h = 20 min. So in 50 min he is
steps.margin_note: Show the 30 + 20 = 50 min first — it proves the round trip fits the interval exactly.
steps.why: Average velocity reads only the endpoints. He ends where he started, so the displacement — and with it the average velocity — is zero.
common_mistakes: Averaging 5 and 7.5 to get the velocity.

recall.must_convey: That he is back home in exactly 50 min, so the average velocity is zero.
accept: displacement is zero so velocity is zero
thirty plus twenty is fifty minutes

steps.label: Average speed
steps.margin_note: 50 min = 5/6 h. Distance counts BOTH legs; that is what separates it from velocity.
steps.why: Speed reads the whole path walked, 5 km, over the 5/6 hour it took — the same trip that gave zero velocity gives 6 km/h speed.
common_mistakes: Averaging 5 and 7.5 to get 6.25 — time is not split equally between the legs.

recall.must_convey: That the average speed is 5 km over 5/6 h = 6 km/h.
